Bug_Details:
Category: Perf regression. Reported as "Inefficient Keyset Iterator" by inefficient-keyset-iterator.

This issue is raised when

iterating over a HashMap with keySet() iterator
looking up the key each time

Example:

void inefficient_loop_bad(HashMap<String, Integer> testMap) { for (String key : testMap.keySet()) {   Integer value = testMap.get(key); // extra look-up cost   foo(key, value); }}

Action:

Instead, it is more efficient to iterate over the loop with entrySet which returns key-vaue pairs and gets rid of the hashMap lookup.

void efficient_loop_ok(HashMap<String, Integer> testMap) {  for (Map.Entry<String, Integer> entry : testMap.entrySet()) {    String key = entry.getKey();    Integer value = entry.getValue();    foo(key, value);  }}
Bug_Explanation: The bug is related to performance regression due to inefficient iteration over a HashMap using keySet(). The code iterates over the keys and performs a lookup on each key to retrieve the value, causing extra lookup cost. The more efficient approach would be using entrySet() to directly access key-value pairs.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case 'testShowBug' calls the 'showBug' method of the class 'InefficientKeySetIteratorExample', which internally calls the 'inefficientLoopBad' method. This method iterates over the testMap using keySet() and looks up each key, triggering the performance-related bug by causing inefficient iteration and extra lookup cost.
